title: Valproate — Pediatric Status Epilepticus (Second-Line)
sources: Chamberlain JM, et al. ESETT — Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications for Status Epilepticus. NEJM. 2019;381:2103-2113.
Glauser T, et al. Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults — AES 2016.
Drug_Dosing_Peds_Weight_Based_Spec.md (cross-checked vs Stanford & Riley Children's pathways).

changelog.change: Initial entry — one of the second/third-line agents named in peds-lorazepam-status's buildNote as the still-needed remainder of the status-epilepticus set.

purpose: Second-line agent for pediatric status epilepticus persisting after an adequate benzodiazepine dose — roughly equivalent efficacy to fosphenytoin and levetiracetam per ESETT; avoid where hepatotoxicity or a mitochondrial disorder is a concern.

doses.notes: Infuse over ~10 minutes (the ESETT protocol infusion time).

contraindications: Known or suspected mitochondrial disease (POLG mutation) — risk of fulminant hepatic failure
Known hepatic disease or significant hepatic impairment
Pregnancy (teratogenicity) — rarely a factor in the acute pediatric status setting but worth noting for adolescent patients
Age < 2 years is a relative caution — higher reported hepatotoxicity risk in this group; many protocols prefer fosphenytoin or levetiracetam first in infants and toddlers
buildNote: Second/third-line status-epilepticus sibling of peds-lorazepam-status and peds-midazolam-status. ESETT (2019) found valproate, fosphenytoin (see peds-fosphenytoin-status), and levetiracetam (see peds-levetiracetam-status) roughly equivalent in efficacy (~45-50% seizure cessation) and safety when benzodiazepines fail — choice is largely institutional preference and contraindication profile, not a clear winner.
